target.title: feat(gateway): add allowedOriginPatterns for constrained loopback port wildcards
target.body:
Closes #98383

## What Problem This Solves

Remote WebView-hosted node clients (e.g. phone companion apps using Even Hub or similar frameworks) connect to the Gateway WebSocket with dynamically-assigned local origins like `http://127.0.0.1:<random-port>`. The current `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins` only supports exact origins or the global `["*"]` wildcard, forcing users to choose between two inadequate options:

- **Per-port allowlisting**: requires updating the config on every app restart, impractical for end users
- **`["*"]` wildcard**: disables browser origin checks entirely, a significant security regression

## Why This Change Was Made

Added `gateway.controlUi.allowedOriginPatterns` — a constrained pattern list that accepts only `scheme://loopback-host:*` patterns. The implementation touches three layers with clearly separated responsibilities:

**1. Zod schema (config load time — fail-close)**

Each pattern must pass six checks: valid format (`scheme://host:*`), explicit protocol (`http:` or `https:`), port-level `*` wildcard only, no host wildcards, and hostname in the loopback literal set (`127.0.0.1`, `localhost`, `[::1]`). Illegal patterns prevent service startup — no silent downgrades.

**2. Runtime matching (`checkBrowserOrigin`)**

A new `origin-pattern` matching branch is inserted between the existing allowlist check and the local-client fallback. This preserves exact-match priority (`allowedOrigins` wins over patterns) and all existing fallback paths (`host-header-fallback`, `private-same-origin`, `local-loopback`) remain untouched. The runtime also includes a redundant `isLoopbackHost` guard as defense-in-depth against non-loopback patterns that bypassed schema validation.

**3. Startup config validation**

- `server-runtime-config.ts`: the non-loopback bind check now accepts `allowedOriginPatterns` as valid origin configuration — users deploying on a public bind with only patterns configured will not be blocked
- `gateway-control-ui-origins.ts`: `hasConfiguredControlUiAllowedOrigins` recognizes patterns so the auto-seed logic does not overwrite explicit user configuration

**4. Codex review follow-up**

- `schema.help.ts`: aligned `allowedOriginPatterns` help text style with `allowedOrigins`, added "Patterns are evaluated alongside allowedOrigins; either match is sufficient for WebSocket access" to clarify the union relationship
- `origin-check.test.ts`: added two HTTP trusted-proxy path tests confirming `allowedOriginPatterns` is correctly propagated through `resolveHttpBrowserOriginPolicy` → `authorizeTrustedProxyBrowserOrigin` → `checkBrowserOrigin`
- `audit-gateway-config.ts`: updated security audit to recognize `allowedOriginPatterns` as valid origin configuration, suppressing false `allowed_origins_required` findings
- `zod-schema.ts`: added `.describe()` metadata for `allowedOriginPatterns`
- `schema.help.ts`: updated `allowedOrigins` help text to reference `allowedOriginPatterns` as a safer alternative for dynamic loopback port clients
- `docs/gateway/configuration-reference.md` and `docs/gateway/troubleshooting.md`: added `allowedOriginPatterns` to public docs and origin-error remediation guidance

**Design constraints preserved across the stack:**

- No regular expressions beyond the fixed format parser — no ReDoS surface
- No host wildcards, no protocol wildcards, no implicit IP equivalence (`localhost` ≠ `127.0.0.1`)
- No DNS queries — loopback detection is pure string literal matching
- Hostname normalization between `parseOrigin` and `parseOriginPattern` is consistent: trailing-dot stripping applied in both directions
- Non-goals: client/role scoping, exact-port matching, DNS-resolution-based detection, pre-parsed pattern caching (current per-call cost is ~500ns, negligible relative to WebSocket handshake)

## User Impact

Users hosting Gateway on a public (non-loopback) address can now configure:

```json
{
  "gateway": {
    "controlUi": {
      "allowedOriginPatterns": ["http://127.0.0.1:*"]
    }
  }
}
```

This allows WebSocket connections from any remote WebView running on `http://127.0.0.1:<any-port>` without resorting to `["*"]`. The full loopback family is supported (`127.0.0.1`, `localhost`, `[::1]`, both `http:` and `https:` protocols).

**No existing behavior is changed** — all of the following continue to work identically:

- `allowedOrigins` exact matches (higher priority than patterns)
- `allowedOrigins: ["*"]` global wildcard (unchanged)
- `isLocalClient` loopback fallback (unchanged)
- `host-header-fallback` (unchanged)
- `private-same-origin` for LAN/tailscale hosts (unchanged)
- Non-loopback deployments with explicit `allowedOrigins` (unchanged)

Users currently on `["*"]` for WebView support can migrate to `["http://127.0.0.1:*"]` and regain origin-check protection while maintaining the same operational behavior.

**Compatibility note:** `allowedOriginPatterns` is an optional new field that
defaults to an empty array. Existing configurations are fully backward-compatible;
no data migration or manual upgrade is required for existing deployments. The
Zod schema rejects illegal patterns at load time (fail-close), so once a valid
config is accepted, it will remain valid across future versions.

## Evidence

**Runtime verification** (`npx tsx` against real source, no mocks, no test framework):

```
30/30 tests passed

─── A: Zod Schema allowedOriginPatterns (11/11) ───
  ✅ A1: http://127.0.0.1:* accepted
  ✅ A2: http://localhost:* accepted
  ✅ A3: http://[::1]:* accepted
  ✅ A4: https://127.0.0.1:* accepted
  ✅ A5: non-loopback hostname rejected
  ✅ A6: exact port without * rejected
  ✅ A7: host wildcard http://*:* rejected
  ✅ A8: bare * rejected
  ✅ A9: ftp protocol rejected
  ✅ A10: empty patterns array accepted (no regression)
  ✅ A11: allowedOrigins + allowedOriginPatterns coexist

─── B: checkBrowserOrigin runtime matching (15/15) ───
  ✅ B1: http://127.0.0.1:40313 matches pattern [CORE ISSUE SCENARIO]
  ✅ B2: http://localhost:5173 matches http://localhost:*
  ✅ B3: http://[::1]:8080 matches http://[::1]:*
  ✅ B4: https://127.0.0.1:9000 matches https://127.0.0.1:*
  ✅ B5: http://127.0.0.1 (no explicit port) matches pattern
  ✅ B6: non-loopback origin blocked
  ✅ B7: localhost != 127.0.0.1 (no implicit equivalence)
  ✅ B8: protocol mismatch rejected
  ✅ B9: allowedOrigins exact match takes priority over patterns
  ✅ B10: existing * wildcard still works (no regression)
  ✅ B11: isLocalClient loopback fallback unchanged (no regression)
  ✅ B12: empty patterns does not create bypass
  ✅ B13: trailing dot normalization works (localhost. matches localhost)
  ✅ B14: first matching pattern in array wins
  ✅ B15: * in allowedOrigins + empty patterns still works

─── C: CSRF startup guard (4/4) ───
  ✅ C1: allowedOriginPatterns counts as configured origins
  ✅ C2: both empty → not configured (CSRF guard active)
  ✅ C3: allowedOrigins with values still works
  ✅ C4: host-header fallback still works
```

**Regression test suites** (vitest, all passing):

| Test suite | Result |
|-----------|--------|
| `src/gateway/origin-check.test.ts` | 136/136 passed |
| `src/gateway/server-runtime-config.test.ts` | 58/58 passed |
| `src/gateway/server.auth.browser-hardening.test.ts` | 28/28 passed |
| `src/security/audit-gateway-exposure.test.ts` | 16/16 passed |
| **Total** | **238/238 passed** |

<details>
<summary>Real Gateway/WebSocket end-to-end verification</summary>

Test config openclaw.json

        "http://127.0.0.1:*",
        "http://localhost:*"
      ],
      "dangerouslyAllowHostHeaderOriginFallback": false
    }
  }
}
